guideTitle: 6 Best Outdoor Motion Sensor Light Bulbs in 2026
metaTitle: Best Outdoor Motion Sensor Light Bulbs 2026
metaDescription: Six outdoor motion sensor light bulbs compared on lumens, sensing range, dusk-to-dawn control and base type, so you can upgrade a porch or garage light.
introParagraphs: A motion sensor bulb is the laziest way to upgrade an outdoor light. You unscrew the old bulb, screw in the new one, and the porch, garage entry or side path wakes up when someone approaches. There is no switch to rewire and no new fixture to hang, which is why these bulbs appeal to people who want security lighting without a project.

The six picks cover standard A19 and A21 shapes, a PAR38 floodlight style from GE, and a few bulbs with a built-in dusk to dawn photocell. Brightness runs from 800 lumens up to 1100 lumens, and detection reaches roughly 8 to 24 feet depending on the model. The right pick depends on your fixture shape, the weather exposure and how far from the door the bulb sits.
We evaluated each bulb based on product specs and buyer feedback, comparing lumen output, base, sensing range and daylight control. This is a reading of the published numbers, not a weather trial.

products.name: Torkase E26 Motion Sensor Light Bulb
products.description:
Torkase takes the top spot because it combines the highest brightness in the lineup, 1100 lumens, with a clean feature list. It is described as a 100W equivalent LED and is rated for 20,000 hours. A PIR motion sensor detects movement within 8 to 16 feet, and a dusk to dawn function keeps it from lighting in daytime.

The bulb is aimed at security use, and its pitch is that it illuminates when someone approaches. Because it is a standard E26 bulb, it fits most common sockets, so you can use it on a porch lamp or a garage fixture with no modification. A bright 1100 lumens is generous for a covered entry, though it can flood a small porch.

Its range of 8 to 16 feet is middling next to the 24 feet that GE lists for its A21 model, so a long driveway is not its natural home. Compared with the 13W OHLUX, it gives similar light with a more detailed spec sheet. For most front doors and garage entries, it is the easiest upgrade here.
products.bestFor: Front doors and garage entries that want the brightest bulb swap.

products.name: GE LED+ PAR38 Motion Sensor Floodlight Bulbs
products.description:
GE gives you the only floodlight shaped bulb in this comparison, a 15W PAR38 sold as a 2 pack in warm white. It screws into any fixture that fits an E26 medium base, and the light turns on as soon as the power is on. An advanced motion sensor offers a 90 degree viewing angle, which is narrower than the wide arcs of some competitors.

A floodlight bulb is designed to push light forward, so it works well in recessed cans and spotlight fixtures that aim at a driveway or yard. GE also makes an A21 version, which lists detection within 24 feet and damp-rated construction, so check which shape fits your fitting. The two pack is handy when you have a front and back door.

The warm white tone is easier on the eyes than the cooler daylight of the Aovpex, though it is less stark for security. Compared with the Torkase at 1100 lumens, you are choosing a directional flood over an all-around bulb. It is the right choice when your fixture is already a spotlight style.

products.name: Aovpex 100W Equivalent Motion Sensor Bulbs
products.description:
The Aovpex is a straightforward 100W equivalent bulb with a daylight color tone and plug and play installation. Its sensor detects heat waves radiating from moving objects and then turns on the light when movement is detected. A dusk to dawn feature deactivates motion detection when ambient light is above 40 lux and reactivates it in the dark.

That 40 lux figure is useful because it tells you how dim the surroundings must be before it fires. A bright porch lamp, a street light or a nearby window can keep the bulb from ever waking, so placement matters. It is described as suitable for indoor and outdoor use, which gives it flexibility in a garage, hallway or entry.

The brief lacks a lumen rating and a range figure, so you are buying mostly on the 100W equivalent claim. Next to the Torkase, which spells out 1100 lumens and 8 to 16 ft, the Aovpex is less documented. It is a reasonable pick if you want a daylight color bulb and are comfortable with fewer published specs.

products.name: GREENIC 9W A19 Motion Sensor Light Bulb
products.description:
GREENIC publishes the most complete sensing detail of the group. Its A19 bulb is 9W, 60W equivalent and 800 lumens at 5000K, with a PIR sensor that reaches 10 to 13 ft. It also states a detection height range of 6.8 to 8 ft, which tells you how far above the ground the bulb should sit.

That height figure is the kind of fact most buyers miss. If the bulb is mounted too low or too high, the sensor field may not cross the path you want, and the instructions note it must be installed within the right band. A built-in photocell keeps the bulb off during the day, which saves power and avoids needless triggers.

At 800 lumens it is noticeably dimmer than the 1100 lumen Torkase, but it matches the Sylvania at 800 lumens. A 10 to 13 ft range fits a front step or side gate more than a long driveway. If you like having exact numbers, this is the best documented bulb in the lineup.

products.name: OHLUX 13W Dusk to Dawn Motion Light Bulb
products.description:
OHLUX uses a dual-sensor design with a high sensitivity PIR infrared motion sensor and a dusk to dawn photocell. The bulb draws 13W and is rated as a 100W equivalent in daylight tone. It lights up on motion at night and turns off 45 seconds after movement stops.

That 45 second figure is a useful number because it tells you exactly how long the light lingers. It is long enough to carry a bag from the car to the door, and short enough that the bulb does not stay lit all night. The dual-sensor combination means it does not fire in daytime, which protects against false triggers from sunlit branches.

The brief does not list a lumen figure, so you are choosing based on the 100W equivalent claim. Compared with the Torkase at 1100 lumens, the OHLUX is similar in intent but less documented, and against the Aovpex it is more specific about timing. It is a good choice for a porch where you want predictable behaviour.

products.name: Sylvania A19 Dusk to Dawn Motion Sensor Bulb
products.description:
The Sylvania stands out for color quality, offering a 90 CRI rating alongside 800 lumens of 5000K daylight light. It draws 8.5W as a replacement for a 60W incandescent, and the frosted finish softens the glare. Its motion sensing turns it on automatically for homes, garages, porches, entryways and similar areas.

A high CRI means colors under the light look more natural, which is useful when you check a package, a license plate or a garden. It also supports dusk to dawn operation, so it works as a safety light that wakes only after dark. The bulb is a standard A19 shape, which fits ordinary fixtures.

It matches the GREENIC at 800 lumens, but the Sylvania uses less power at 8.5W against 9W. Next to the Torkase it is dimmer, so it suits a covered porch rather than a wide yard. If appearance matters at your door, this is the most refined bulb here.

buyingCriteria.explanation: A watt equivalent is a rough label, while lumens are the real measure of brightness. The Torkase states 1100 lumens, and both the GREENIC and Sylvania state 800 lumens. Bulbs like the OHLUX and Aovpex list only the 100W equivalent, so you must infer their output. For a front door under a roof, 800 lumens is often enough, and for an open yard 1100 lumens is a safer target. If the listing hides lumens, consider that a reason to compare more carefully.

Range tells you how far ahead the bulb sees, and mounting height decides whether the sensor field crosses your path. The Torkase lists 8 to 16 feet, the GREENIC 10 to 13 ft with a 6.8 to 8 ft height, and the GE A21 lists 24 feet. A short range is fine for a step or porch, but a long walkway wants more reach. Because PIR reacts to crossing heat, mount the bulb so people walk across its view rather than straight into it. Check your fixture height before buying.

A photocell makes sure the bulb does not trigger during the day. The Aovpex deactivates motion detection above 40 lux, the OHLUX pairs PIR with a dusk sensor, and the Sylvania and Torkase also include dusk to dawn behaviour. Without it, a sunlit branch moving in the breeze could wear out the bulb or waste power. Remember that bright neighbouring lights can keep a bulb off at night too. Place it where ambient light is truly dark.

A bulb is not a fixture, so rain exposure depends on the housing it sits in. The GE A21 is listed as damp-rated, but you should still use a covered or enclosed fixture for any bulb, including the Torkase, OHLUX and GREENIC. Bare bulbs facing open weather risk moisture getting into the base or the sensor. Check the product listing for damp or wet ratings, and shelter the bulb under an eave. A porch lantern with a glass cover is a safe place.

Almost every bulb here uses an E26 base, but the shape matters. The GE PAR38 is a floodlight shape that suits recessed cans and spotlight heads, while the Torkase, GREENIC, OHLUX and Sylvania are A19 or A21 style bulbs. A bulb with a sensor dome is larger than an ordinary one, so confirm it fits inside a tight lantern. If a fixture has a narrow neck, the sensor may be blocked. Measure first if the housing is enclosed.

Cool daylight light feels like security light, and warm white feels more welcoming. The GE PAR38 is warm white, while the GREENIC and Sylvania are 5000K. The Sylvania's 90 CRI makes colors look more natural, which helps when you identify objects. If your porch is part of the home's look, choose warmer light. If it is purely for safety, a crisp daylight tone is fine.

howWeEvaluated.title: Brightness delivered
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared stated lumens where published, from the Torkase at 1100 lumens to the GREENIC and Sylvania at 800 lumens. Bulbs that only quote a 100W equivalent were marked lower confidence. Brightness was weighed against realistic use, such as a covered porch or an open yard.

howWeEvaluated.title: Sensor detail
howWeEvaluated.description: Detection range, height and angle were read from each listing, including the GREENIC's 10 to 13 ft and 6.8 to 8 ft height and the GE's 90 degree angle. Bulbs that publish more figures scored higher, because buyers can plan placement. We noted that PIR sensing reacts best to crossing movement.

howWeEvaluated.title: Daylight control
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at dusk to dawn behaviour, such as the Aovpex's 40 lux cutoff and the OHLUX's dual sensors. A bulb that stays quiet in daytime saves power and avoids false triggers. Bulbs without clear daylight control would have lost points.

howWeEvaluated.title: Fixture fit
howWeEvaluated.description: We checked base type and shape, from the standard E26 base to the GE PAR38 flood style. Fit determines whether you can swap the bulb without changing the fixture. Weather exposure was considered separately, since all bulbs need shelter.

howWeEvaluated.title: Lineup positioning
howWeEvaluated.description: The Torkase leads on brightness at 1100 lumens, the GE PAR38 leads on floodlight shape, and the GREENIC leads on documented sensing detail. The OHLUX leads on a known 45 second timing, and the Sylvania leads on color rendering with a 90 CRI. The Aovpex sits as a plug-and-play daylight option.

faq.q: Can I use a motion sensor bulb in any outdoor fixture?
faq.a: Not necessarily. The bulb needs the right base and enough space for its sensor dome. Most use an E26 base, but a tight lantern may block the sensor. Use an enclosed or covered fixture to shelter the bulb from rain.

faq.q: How bright should an outdoor motion bulb be?
faq.a: For a covered porch, 800 lumens from the GREENIC or Sylvania is usually enough. For a wider area, the Torkase at 1100 lumens gives more output. Some bulbs, like the OHLUX and Aovpex, list only a 100W equivalent.

faq.q: Why does my bulb not turn on during the day?
faq.a: Dusk to dawn bulbs are designed to stay off in daylight. The Aovpex deactivates motion detection above 40 lux, for example. If it stays off at night, check for nearby bright lights.

faq.q: Do motion sensor bulbs last as long as regular LEDs?
faq.a: The Torkase is rated for 20,000 hours, which is comparable to many LED bulbs. The sensor electronics add some complexity, so lifespan can vary. Shelter from weather helps.

faq.q: Where should I mount the bulb for best detection?
faq.a: Follow the height and range the listing gives. The GREENIC specifies a 6.8 to 8 ft height and a 10 to 13 ft range. Place it so people cross the sensor's view instead of walking straight at it.

faq.q: Is a floodlight bulb better than a standard one?
faq.a: It depends on the fixture. A PAR38 like the GE aims light forward and suits spotlight heads. A standard A19 shape spreads light all around and suits lanterns.
